issues.title: fix(ui): prepare VPN configuration before tray connections
issues.body:
## Issue

On a fresh installation, clicking **Connect** in the tray icon's menu can crash AmneziaVPN if the user has not connected through the main window yet. Connecting through the main window once makes subsequent tray connections work.

## Env & version

- OS: Omarchy 4.0.6 (Arch Linux based)
- Desktop: Hyprland
- Kernel: 7.2.15-1-omarchy
- AmneziaVPN: 5.1.0.6

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install AmneziaVPN on a machine where it has not been used before.
2. Launch the application and add your VPN configuration.
3. Do **not** click **Connect** in the main application window.
4. Right-click the AmneziaVPN tray icon in the top bar.
5. Click **Connect** in the context menu.

**Actual:** AmneziaVPN crashes. This was reproduced twice on the affected installation.

**Expected:** AmneziaVPN prepares the selected connection and connects, or displays an error if it cannot proceed.

**Workaround:** Relaunch AmneziaVPN, open its main window, and connect there once. After this, connecting from the tray menu works.

## Root Cause

The tray's **Connect** action skips the checks and setup performed by the main window's **Connect** button. It tries to start the VPN immediately, even when the connection configuration is not ready. The crash dump shows the app trying to use a missing configuration handler.

## Fix

- Change the tray connection in `coreSignalHandlers.cpp` to call `ConnectionUiController::toggleConnection()` instead of `openConnection()`.
- This reuses the main window's existing validation and configuration preparation before starting the VPN.
- Add regression tests for tray Connect with an unprepared server and while connection preparation is already in progress.

## Validation

- Confirmed the original crash with a local core dump and traced the tray action in the source.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Qt `moc` processed the updated test file and registered both new test cases.
- Full build, regression test execution, and verification of the patched app have not been performed.

issues.title: Linux: NetworkManager CONNECTED_GLOBAL transition causes unnecessary full VPN reconnect
issues.body:
# Linux: NetworkManager CONNECTED_GLOBAL transition causes unnecessary full VPN reconnect and recreates tun2

## Describe the bug

On Linux, AmneziaVPN performs a full VPN reconnect whenever NetworkManager emits:

```text
StateChanged(NM_STATE_CONNECTED_GLOBAL = 70)
```

even when the physical network, Wi-Fi access point, interface, and gateway have not actually changed.

A normal NetworkManager connectivity transition:

```text
CONNECTED_GLOBAL -> CONNECTED_SITE -> CONNECTED_GLOBAL
```

is interpreted by AmneziaVPN as a network change.

When NetworkManager returns to `CONNECTED_GLOBAL`, AmneziaVPN calls `VpnConnection::reconnectToVpn()`. With Xray this stops Xray/tun2socks, destroys `tun2`, and creates a new tunnel.

In my case the event is triggered periodically by NetworkManager connectivity checks. The Wi-Fi access point does not change.

The unnecessary reconnect is disruptive by itself, but the reconnect cleanup also sometimes fails, leaving DNS/routes in a broken state until a manual VPN reconnect.

## Environment

* OS: Ubuntu 25.10
* Kernel: Linux 6.17.0-41-generic
* Network manager: NetworkManager
* VPN protocol: Xray
* Xray data path: `tun2` + `tun2socks`
* TUN address: `10.33.0.2/24`
* Physical connection remains active during the reproduced event

## Reproduced timeline

Incident captured on 2026-08-31.

### NetworkManager changes connectivity classification

```text
16:30:05.947  DNS query: connectivity-check.ubuntu.com A
16:30:06.312  DNS reply: NOERROR
16:30:06.628  NetworkManager state is now CONNECTED_SITE
16:30:06.xxx  Amnezia LinuxNetworkWatcherWorker: NMStateChanged 60
```

NetworkManager then retries connectivity checks.

Approximately 31 seconds later:

```text
16:30:37.338  DNS reply: NOERROR
16:30:37.657  NetworkManager state is now CONNECTED_GLOBAL
16:30:37.658  Amnezia LinuxNetworkWatcherWorker:
               Properties changed for interface org.freedesktop.NetworkManager.Device
16:30:37.658  Amnezia LinuxNetworkWatcherWorker:
               Access point did not changed. Ignoring the changes
16:30:37.658  Amnezia LinuxNetworkWatcherWorker:
               NMStateChanged 70
```

The important part is that AmneziaVPN itself reports that the access point did not change.

### AmneziaVPN immediately reconnects

Immediately after `NMStateChanged 70`:

```text
AmneziaVPN.desktop:
Reconnect triggered. Reconnecting to the server

AmneziaVPN.desktop:
XrayProtocol::stop()
```

The existing TUN is then removed:

```text
NetworkManager:
device (tun2): state change: activated -> unmanaged
(reason 'unmanaged', managed-type: 'removed')

AmneziaVPN-service:
deleteTun ret 0
```

The diagnostic bundle independently confirms that the TUN FD was owned by Amnezia's `tun2socks` process.

### Cleanup errors

During this automatic reconnect the logs also contain:

```text
Failed to delete tun
No suitable DNS manager found.
VpnConnection::onConnectionStateChanged: Failed to flush DNS
Failed to clear saved routes
```

and several route deletion failures.

A `pkill` invocation also reports:

```text
pkill: pattern that searches for process name longer than 15 characters
will result in zero matches
Try `pkill -f' ...
```

### Tunnel is recreated

AmneziaVPN then starts Xray/tun2socks again and creates a new TUN:

```text
XrayProtocol::start()
Xray::startXray()

tun2socks -device tun://tun2 -proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:...

ip tuntap add mode tun dev tun2
ip addr add 10.33.0.2/24 dev tun2
ip link set dev tun2 up
```

Therefore the `tun2` deletion is not caused by NetworkManager. NetworkManager observes the externally managed interface disappearing.

The tunnel is deliberately torn down by AmneziaVPN as part of `reconnectToVpn()`.

## Source-code cause

### Describe the bug

On macOS, an XRay (VLESS + Reality) profile whose server address is a **domain name** never establishes: the app reaches "Connected", the `utun` interface is created but **never receives an IP address**, no traffic flows, and networking stays broken until disconnect. On disconnect the log shows `Failed to stop xray`.

Replacing only the server address with the server's **literal IPv4** (same key, same Reality parameters, same SNI) makes the very same profile work: `utun` gets its address and traffic flows.

### To Reproduce

1. Self-host xray-core (26.3.x), VLESS + Reality on TCP 443, with a DNS A record pointing at the server.
2. On macOS, import a `vpn://` key (or `vless://` link) where the outbound `vnext.address` is the **domain name**.
3. Connect. The app shows "Connected", but `ifconfig` shows the new `utun` interface without an inet address; nothing loads, the machine effectively loses networking until disconnect.
4. Re-import the same profile with `vnext.address` set to the server's literal IPv4 — it works: the `utun` gets its address (e.g. `10.x.x.x`) and traffic flows through the server.

A domain endpoint should work: resolve the name **before** the tunnel takes over the default route (or add a bypass route for the resolved IP once known). Otherwise the resolver query is routed into the tunnel that is still being established — a chicken-and-egg loop that can never complete.

### Evidence that it is the resolution order

- The same domain-based profile works in AmneziaVPN on **iOS**: the Network Extension excludes the provider's own traffic, so the name resolves outside the tunnel.
- The same domain-based `vless://` link works on the same Mac in a third-party client (V2Box), which resolves the name before route setup and adds a host bypass route for the resolved address.
- The "Use AmneziaDNS" toggle has no effect on this (tested both ways).
- Not a duplicate of #2722: there the tunnel comes up and passes IP traffic while in-tunnel DNS fails; here the tunnel never comes up at all when the address is a domain.

- **OS:** macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6)
- **AmneziaVPN Client Version:** 4.8.15.4 and 5.0.2.0 (both reproduce)
- **Protocol:** XRay, VLESS + Reality over TCP 443, self-hosted xray-core 26.3.x

issues.title: fix(android): skip split tunneling apps that are not installed
issues.body:
## Summary

Skip app split tunneling entries for packages that are not installed instead of crashing the VPN service.

## Problem

`Protocol.buildVpnInterface()` calls `VpnService.Builder.addAllowedApplication()` / `addDisallowedApplication()` for every package in the app split tunneling list. Both throw `PackageManager.NameNotFoundException` when the package is not installed. Nothing catches it: `AmneziaVpnService.connectionExceptionHandler` does not list it and rethrows, so the `:amnezia*Service` process dies.

The list easily contains such entries: an app that was uninstalled after being added, or a backup restored on another device. The service is restarted with the same config (`START_REDELIVER_INTENT`, Always-on), so the crash repeats until the user finds and removes the entry.

## Changes

- Catch `NameNotFoundException` around each call, log a warning with the package name and continue, the same way `AppListProvider` handles missing packages.

In *Only apps from the list* mode, if every listed package is missing, no application filter is set and all traffic goes through the VPN, which fails safe.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`
- Not built locally: I don't have an Android toolchain set up. The change is limited to the two loops in `Protocol.kt` and one import.

issues.title: fix(windows): fail WireGuard activation when the kill switch cannot be enabled
issues.body:
## Summary

Stop a WireGuard/AmneziaWG connection on Windows from reporting *Connected* when the kill switch could not be set up.

## Problem

`WireguardUtilsWindows::addInterface()` ignores the result of `WindowsFirewall::enableInterface()`, and `updatePeer()` ignores the result of `WindowsFirewall::enablePeerTraffic()`.

When any `FwpmFilterAdd0` call inside `enablePeerTraffic()` fails (for example with a long split tunneling list), its scope guard aborts the transaction and calls `disableKillSwitch()`. In the default mode that removes every filter, yet activation continues and the client shows *Connected* with the kill switch enabled in settings while no filters are installed.

## Changes

- Return `false` from `addInterface()` and `updatePeer()` when the firewall call fails, with an error in the log.

`Daemon::activate()` already handles a `false` from both methods (it is the path a failed route takes), and `WindowsDaemon` disables the kill switch on `activationFailure`, so the user gets a failed connection instead of an unprotected one.

## Backward compatibility

Nothing changes when the firewall calls succeed or when the kill switch is off.

## Verification

- Built the Windows x64 client, service and tests in Release mode (MSVC 19.35, Qt 6.10.1) against `dev` at ac175c8; `ctest` passes.
- Checked that both firewall methods return `false` only on WFP API errors: an empty IPv6 gateway becomes a valid `::` filter, so there is no new failure for configs that connect today.

issues.title: fix(daemon): clear host bits in allowed IP ranges
issues.body:
## Summary

Clear the host bits of allowed IP ranges when the daemon parses the activation config, so a split tunneling entry such as `104.16.0.1/12` no longer breaks WireGuard/AmneziaWG connections on Windows.

## Problem

Site split tunneling accepts entries like `192.168.1.10/24`: `NetworkUtilities::checkIpSubnetFormat()` only checks the syntax, and `LocalSocketController::activate()` splits `address/range` and sends both parts unchanged. `Daemon::parseConfig()` then builds each range with `IPAddress(QHostAddress, int)`, which keeps the host bits.

On Windows such a range reaches `CreateIpForwardEntry2` as is. Windows rejects a destination prefix with host bits set:

```text
198.51.100.7/24 -> CreateIpForwardEntry2 = 87 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER)
198.51.100.0/24 -> CreateIpForwardEntry2 = 0
```

`updateRoutePrefix()` returns `false`, and `Daemon::activate()` aborts the whole connection because of that one entry. With the kill switch on, `WindowsFirewall::blockTrafficTo()` also uses `address()` as the lower bound of the WFP range, so the block for `1.2.3.4/24` starts at `.4` instead of `.0`.

`excludedAddresses` already go through `IPAddress(QString)`, which uses `QHostAddress::parseSubnet()` and clears the host bits.

## Changes

- Build allowed ranges with `IPAddress(QString)` so they are normalized the same way as excluded addresses:

```text
104.16.0.1/12  -> 104.16.0.0/12
192.168.1.10/24 -> 192.168.1.0/24
8.8.8.8/32     -> 8.8.8.8/32
2001:db8::1/32 -> 2001:db8::/32
```

## Backward compatibility

Ranges without host bits are unchanged. The UAPI `allowed_ip` lines, routes and firewall ranges now describe the same network.

## Verification

- Built the Windows x64 client, service and tests in Release mode (MSVC 19.35, Qt 6.10.1) against `dev` at ac175c8; `ctest` passes.
- Checked the `parseSubnet` results above and the `CreateIpForwardEntry2` results above with standalone programs (the test route was added on the loopback interface and removed).

issues.title: fix(windows): run ipconfig /flushdns with separate arguments
issues.body:
## Summary

Make `RouterWin::flushDns()` actually run `ipconfig /flushdns`.

## Problem

`flushDns()` passes the whole command line to `QProcess::start(command)`. In Qt 6 the single-string overload treats its argument as the program name, so Qt looks for an executable called `ipconfig /flushdns`, fails to start it and the method still returns `true`. The service calls `flushDns` on every connect and disconnect (`VpnConnection::onConnectionStateChanged`) and after re-resolving split tunneling sites, so cached DNS answers from before the tunnel came up were never dropped.

A standalone check against Qt 6.10.1 on Windows:

```text
start("ipconfig /flushdns")       -> waitForStarted() = false, error = FailedToStart
start("ipconfig", {"/flushdns"})  -> waitForStarted() = true,  exitCode = 0
```

## Changes

- Start `ipconfig` with `/flushdns` as a separate argument, the same way `RouterLinux` starts `systemctl`.

## Not changed

`RouterWin::resetIpStack()` has the same pattern for `netsh int ip reset` and `netsh winsock reset`, so those commands never run either. It is called on every connect, and both commands reset the Windows network stack and need a reboot to take effect, so making them run would be a behaviour change of its own. I left it as is.

## Verification

- Built the Windows x64 client, service and tests in Release mode (MSVC 19.35, Qt 6.10.1) against `dev` at ac175c8; `ctest` passes.
- Confirmed the `QProcess` behaviour above with a standalone Qt program.

issues.title: fix(settings): restore split tunneling route modes saved as strings
issues.body:
## Summary

Keep the site and app split tunneling route modes when restoring a backup that was created on Linux or Android.

## Problem

On Linux and Android `QSettings` uses the INI format, which does not keep value types, so `SecureQSettings::backupAppConfig()` writes `Conf/routeMode` and `Conf/appsRouteMode` as JSON strings (for example `"2"`). `SettingsController::restoreAppConfigFromData()` reads them with `QJsonValue::toInt()`, which returns `0` for a string, so the restore always emits `RouteMode::VpnAllSites` and `AppsRouteMode::VpnAllApps`.

With site split tunneling enabled, `VpnAllSites` is a mode the rest of the app does not expect:

- `OpenVpnConfigurator::processConfigWithLocalSettings()` removes `redirect-gateway` and has no branch for it, and `VpnConnection::onConnectionStateChanged()` deletes the `0.0.0.0` route without adding any other, so a self-hosted OpenVPN connection reports *Connected* while traffic does not go through the tunnel.
- After the next start `IpSplitTunnelingController` migrates `VpnAllSites` to `VpnOnlyForwardSites`, so a user who had *All sites except* ends up with the opposite mode.
- On Android the app route mode becomes `VpnAllApps`, which reads the empty `AllApps` list, so the restored app list is not applied.

The boolean flags next to these values are already read through `toVariant()` for the same reason.

## Changes

- Read `Conf/routeMode` and `Conf/appsRouteMode` through `toVariant().toInt()`, which handles both numbers and numeric strings.
- Add `testRestoreRouteModeStoredAsString` to `BackupExportImportTest`.

## Backward compatibility

Backups that store the modes as numbers (Windows, macOS) are read exactly as before.

## Verification

- Built the Windows x64 client, service and tests in Release mode (MSVC 19.35, Qt 6.10.1) against `dev` at ac175c8.
- The new test fails on `dev` without the fix and passes with it.
- `ctest`: all tests pass.

## Problem

With **Settings → Connection → Use AmneziaDNS** turned off, the client still connects with AmneziaDNS (`172.29.172.254`).

`getDnsPair()` prefers a DNS saved in the server config over the switch:

- `SelfHostedAdminServerConfig::getDnsPair()` checks the switch only when no DNS is saved.

In `ConnectionController::prepareConnection()`, after the DNS pair is resolved for any server type: if the switch is off and the primary DNS is AmneziaDNS, use the user's DNS servers instead.

This is one check where every connection passes, so it covers self-hosted, shared, native and Premium/Free configs. Nothing changes while the switch is on, or when the saved DNS is anything other than AmneziaDNS.

**Describe the bug**
On macOS, when an AmneziaWG server is added by **hostname** (A record only, no AAAA) and the Mac is on a network with **DNS64/NAT64** (e.g. mobile hotspot of a Russian mobile operator), the hostname resolves to a NAT64-synthesized address `64:ff9b::/96`. The macOS daemon then passes it to wireguard-go as `endpoint=<ipv6>:<port>` **without square brackets**, wireguard-go rejects it with IPC error -22, peer creation fails and the connection is immediately dropped (the GUI may sit in "Preparing"/"Connecting").

The same server added by **IPv4 literal** works on the same network. Android client works with the hostname on the same network. Same root cause as the Linux issue #2607, but on macOS and triggered by NAT64 synthesis rather than a real AAAA record.

**Root cause (from source, dev @ 7f9b7db)**
`client/platforms/macos/daemon/wireguardutilsmacos.cpp`, `WireguardUtilsMacos::updatePeer()`:
```cpp
if (!config.m_serverIpv4AddrIn.isNull()) {
    out << "endpoint=" << config.m_serverIpv4AddrIn << ":";      // <- holds 64:ff9b::… here, no brackets
} else if (!config.m_serverIpv6AddrIn.isNull()) {
    out << "endpoint=[" << config.m_serverIpv6AddrIn << "]:";
```
The resolved hostname result ends up in `m_serverIpv4AddrIn` even when it is an IPv6 (NAT64) address. Suggested fix: bracket the address whenever it contains `:` (or put IPv6 results into `m_serverIpv6AddrIn`), and/or prefer A records when resolving the endpoint host.

**To Reproduce**
1. Add a self-hosted AmneziaWG server by hostname that has only an A record (e.g. `relay.example.net` → `203.0.113.10`).
2. Connect the Mac to a DNS64/NAT64 network (mobile hotspot).
3. Click Connect → immediately disconnected.

**Service log** (`/private/var/log/AmneziaVPN/AmneziaVPN-service.log`, key/addresses anonymized)
```
MacosRouteMonitor : Adding exclusion route for 64:ff9b::cb00:710a/128
WireguardUtilsMacos : Configuring peer <pubkey> via 64:ff9b::cb00:710a
WireguardGo : ERROR: (utun4) IPC error -22: failed to set endpoint 64:ff9b::cb00:710a:5275: invalid ip:port "64:ff9b::cb00:710a:5275", IPv6 addresses must be surrounded by square brackets
WireguardUtilsMacos : Peer configuration failed: Unknown error: -22
Daemon : Peer creation failed.
DaemonLocalServerConnection : Failed to activate the interface
```

**Expected behavior**
Connection succeeds (bracketed endpoint `[64:ff9b::cb00:710a]:5275`), or the client uses the A record.

**Environment**
- AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 (de93650), macOS Sequoia 15.7.5 (x86_64)
- Protocol: AmneziaWG, self-hosted server added via hostname

issues.title: [iOS][5.1.0.6] AWG 3.1: connected but no traffic — path-update loop rebinds UDP socket every 2–3 s (works in 5.0.3.0 and AmneziaWG)
issues.body:
## Summary

On iOS, AmneziaVPN **5.1.0.6** connects with an AWG 3.1 profile (handshake confirmed) but no traffic passes. The same profile works in AmneziaVPN **5.0.3.0** and in the **AmneziaWG** app on the same phone.

The tunnel log shows a loop: every 2–3 seconds the network extension handles a "network change", re-applies the endpoint config and rebinds the UDP socket. The interface list does not change between these events.

## Environment

| | Fails | Works | Works |
|---|---|---|---|
| App | AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6 (`ac175c8a8`) | AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 | AmneziaWG (App Store) |
| Device / iOS | iPhone, iOS 26.6.2 | iPhone, iOS 27.2 | same iPhone as "Fails", iOS 26.6.2 |
| Network | LTE (Russian mobile carrier) | LTE, same carrier | LTE, same carrier |
| Profile | same AWG 3.1 profile (self-hosted server, MTU 1280) | same | same |

- The server is a self-hosted AmneziaWG 3.1 server (amneziawg-go). The client receives the handshake response. On the server, the peer's transfer stops after ~16 KB.
- In 5.1.0.6, a profile to a server inside the same country works. Only the server abroad fails. This matches the socket rebind loop: each rebind creates a new UDP flow, and new flows to foreign addresses can be filtered on mobile networks. This part is a hypothesis.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On iOS 26.6.2, install AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6.
2. Import an AWG 3.1 profile (`vpn://`).
3. Connect over LTE.
4. Open any website.

**Expected:** traffic passes, as in 5.0.3.0 and in AmneziaWG.
**Actual:** status is "Connected" and the handshake is confirmed, but no websites load.

## Tunnel log (excerpt, redacted)

```
19:34:14 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - Received handshake response
19:34:16 WG: Observed first handshake at last_handshake_time_sec=...
19:34:18 WG: Network change detected with satisfied route and interface order [pdp_ip0, pdp_ip0, utun8]
19:34:18 WG: Path update state: state=started(...) everHadHandshake=true lastNetworkSettingsUpdateAt=2026-11-04 16:34:14 +0000
19:34:18 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - UAPI: Updating endpoint
19:34:18 WG: UAPI: Updating h1..h4 / s1..s4 padding, header protection key
19:34:18 WG: Routine: receive incoming v4 - stopped
19:34:18 WG: UDP bind has been updated
19:34:18 WG: Routine: receive incoming v4 - started
19:34:18 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - Sending keepalive packet
19:34:21 WG: Network change detected ... [pdp_ip0, pdp_ip0, utun8]   <- same block repeats
19:34:24 ...                                                          <- every 2–3 s
19:34:26 ...
19:34:27 ...
19:34:30 ...
```

`lastNetworkSettingsUpdateAt` does not change, so the app does not re-apply network settings. The path updates come from `NWPathMonitor`. On each update, `WireGuardAdapter.didReceivePathUpdate` (amneziawg-apple v3.1.4) calls `wgSetConfig` and `wgBumpSockets`.

## Analysis

- The two app versions use the same `awg-apple/3.1.4` (see `conanfile.py`). The adapter code is the same.
- One build difference: the `awg-apple` recipe in 5.1.0.6 uses `go/1.27.1` (5.0.3.0 uses `go/1.26.0`).
- The AmneziaWG app on the same phone and iOS version works with the same profile (I did not collect its log). The cause is therefore in the 5.1.0.6 build or the app shell, not in iOS alone.
- I did not find what triggers the repeated path updates in 5.1.0.6.

## Possible fix

In `didReceivePathUpdate`, skip `wgSetConfig` and `wgBumpSockets` when the path has not changed. For example, compare `availableInterfaces` and the status with the last path, and ignore the tunnel's own `utun*` interface.

issues.title: Feature request: import split-tunneling lists via URL/deep link and keep them updated
issues.body:
## Feature request

Please add URL-based import and optional automatic updates for site-based split-tunneling lists, especially on iOS.

This request is about routing lists (domains, IP addresses and CIDR subnets), not subscriptions containing VPN server configurations.

## Use case

I use AmneziaVPN on iOS and want selected destinations to bypass the VPN while all other traffic uses the tunnel.

Currently, distributing and updating an exclusion list requires downloading a JSON file and manually selecting it in the split-tunneling import dialog. If the list changes, each user must repeat this process.

The desired workflow is:

1. A list maintainer publishes a compatible JSON list at a stable HTTPS URL.
2. A user opens an import link (or pastes the HTTPS URL into AmneziaVPN).
3. The app previews the source and routing mode and asks the user to confirm the import.
4. The user can refresh the list manually and optionally enable periodic updates.

This would make it easier to keep the same exclusion list current across devices and share it with family or other users without repeatedly distributing files.

## Proposed behavior

- Import an existing Amnezia site-list JSON file directly from an HTTPS URL.
- Support opening a dedicated deep link or universal link that passes the list URL to AmneziaVPN. The exact link format can be chosen by the maintainers.
- Let the user explicitly select the routing mode. My main use case is "Addresses from the list should not be accessed via VPN"; importing a list should not silently change the existing mode.
- Store the source URL and expose a "Refresh" action, last successful update time, and update errors.
- Offer opt-in automatic refresh, subject to iOS background-execution restrictions; refreshing on app launch or before connection would also be useful.
- Keep downloaded entries associated with their source so that a successful refresh replaces that source's entries, including removals, while preserving independently added local entries.
- Validate the complete response before applying it. On download or validation failure, retain the last successfully imported list.
- Apply updated routes at the next connection if changing them during an active connection is unsupported, and make that behavior clear in the UI.
- Reuse the existing site-list JSON format and supported address types where possible.

A useful first version could support pasting an HTTPS URL and manually refreshing it, with deep links and automatic refresh added later.

## Related work

- #1039 requests additional list formats and automatic downloading/updating of site lists. This request focuses specifically on an HTTPS source, one-link import and its update lifecycle.
- #2449 concerns sharing split-tunneling settings through JSON files.
- #1423 tracks broader improvements to site-based split tunneling.
- PR #2506 proposed server-managed bypass rules and client synchronization, but was closed without merging. Its description explicitly excludes a full subscription/update system for external third-party lists. The workflow requested here would allow a list hosted independently of the VPN server.
- #3298 requests URL subscriptions for VPN server configurations, which is a separate use case.

## Platform

Primary use case: AmneziaVPN on iOS. The same list-source mechanism would also be useful on other platforms.

comments.issue_title: Linux 5.0.1.5: exclusion routes never installed — netlink route dump overflows the   fixed 8 KiB buffer
comments.body:
I can reproduce the missing VPN endpoint exclusion route with **AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6**, build **`ac175c8`**, on **Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, x86_64**. Manually adding a host route through the physical gateway restored connectivity.

### Environment and versions

- Linux clients tested: **5.0.3.0** and **5.1.0.6**. Both exhibited the “connected, but no working traffic” symptom with an AWG 3 server.
- The diagnostics below were collected with **5.1.0.6**.
- Older Linux client **4.8.15.4** worked with my AWG 2 server.
- Mobile client **5.1.0.6** worked with both my AWG 2 and AWG 3 server configurations.
- Docker is installed on the desktop.
- Route counts from `ip -4 route show table all | wc -l` and `ip -6 route show table all | wc -l`: **32 IPv4 routes and 97 IPv6 routes**.

All addresses and physical interface names below are anonymized placeholders.

### Routing observations

With the VPN disconnected, `ip -4 route get MY_SERVER_IP` returned:

```text
MY_SERVER_IP via MY_GATEWAY_IP dev MY_UPLINK_IFACE src MY_HOME_IP
```

With the VPN connected, the same command returned:

```text
MY_SERVER_IP dev amn0 src MY_VPN_IP
```

Only the standard IPv4 routing rules for the `local`, `main`, and `default` tables were present.

In a separate connection attempt to another server (`MY_SECOND_SERVER_IP`), the same Linux client logged:

```text
Adding exclusion route for MY_SECOND_SERVER_IP/32
No default gateway available, skipping exclusion route
```

It subsequently added the full-tunnel routes:

```text
Adding route to 0.0.0.0/1
Adding route to 128.0.0.0/1
```

These are two different VPN servers: the route output and workaround below concern `MY_SERVER_IP`; the log excerpt concerns `MY_SECOND_SERVER_IP`.

### Confirmed workaround

While the VPN was connected, I ran:

```bash
sudo ip -4 route add MY_SERVER_IP/32 via MY_GATEWAY_IP dev MY_UPLINK_IFACE
```

Internet access through the VPN immediately started working. This workaround was verified for `MY_SERVER_IP`.

This appears consistent with the gateway-detection failure discussed in this issue. I have not measured the netlink dump size or tested the proposed patch, so my results confirm the missing endpoint route and the workaround, rather than buffer exhaustion itself.

comments.issue_title: macOS: NAT64-synthesized IPv6 endpoint passed to wireguard-go without brackets → IPC error -22, AmneziaWG can't connect (DNS64 networks)
comments.body:
I can reproduce the same missing-brackets error on macOS, including with a literal IPv6 endpoint rather than a hostname or a DNS64-synthesized address.

Environment:
- AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 (`de93650`, as reported in the log)
- macOS Tahoe 26.6.2, arm64
- Self-hosted AmneziaWG, configuration imported from a `.conf` file

The imported file has a correctly bracketed endpoint, for example:

```ini
Endpoint = [2001:db8:1234:5678::]:34541
```

The address above is a documentation placeholder. The service nevertheless passes the real address to the backend without brackets, producing:

```text
IPC error -22: failed to set endpoint 2001:db8:1234:5678:::34541: invalid ip:port "2001:db8:1234:5678:::34541", IPv6 addresses must be surrounded by square brackets
Peer configuration failed: Unknown error: -22
Peer creation failed.
Failed to activate the interface
```

The UI briefly starts connecting and immediately returns to disconnected. Importing the correctly formatted file as a new profile does not help.

IPv6 was initially disabled for Wi-Fi on this Mac. After enabling automatic IPv6 configuration, a direct TCP connection to the server over IPv6 succeeded, but the app still failed with the error above. The same server and profile then worked on this Mac using the bundled `amneziawg-go` backend with command-line tools (`amneziawg-tools` and the Darwin quick script), bypassing the app's peer configuration path. The server also works over IPv6 from Android.

This suggests the issue also affects literal IPv6 endpoints, not only DNS64/NAT64 resolution.

issues.title: fix(client): bound the wait for the TCP response
issues.body:
Fixes #1682

When fast open is off, `clientImpl.TCP` writes the request and then reads the server's TCP response with no deadline ([client.go#L216](https://github.com/apernet/hysteria/blob/fb25dc852ebbc70658e67889f411887a82b7c281/core/client/client.go#L216)). The server only writes that response after its outbound dial returns ([server.go#L310-L323](https://github.com/apernet/hysteria/blob/fb25dc852ebbc70658e67889f411887a82b7c281/core/server/server.go#L310-L323)). If the server accepts the stream but never answers, while the QUIC connection itself stays alive through keep-alives, the call blocks forever. Because it never returns an error, `reconnectableClientImpl` never sees a `ClosedError` ([reconnect.go#L79-L80](https://github.com/apernet/hysteria/blob/fb25dc852ebbc70658e67889f411887a82b7c281/core/client/reconnect.go#L79-L80)) and so never reconnects.

This change sets a read deadline on the stream only while reading the response, and clears it once the response has arrived. The timeout is `max(MaxIdleTimeout, 30s) + 15s`, which is 45s with the defaults:

- it is longer than the QUIC idle timeout, so a connection that is really dead is still reported by QUIC as it is today;
- it leaves plenty of room for the server-side dial (the direct outbound uses a 10s dial timeout, [ob_direct.go#L21](https://github.com/apernet/hysteria/blob/fb25dc852ebbc70658e67889f411887a82b7c281/extras/outbounds/ob_direct.go#L21)), so a normal slow dial still ends with the server's own error message.

A timeout goes through the existing error path (`wrapIfConnectionClosed`, the same as any other read error on that stream), so the call returns a `ClosedError` and the reconnectable client reconnects on the next call. Fast open is unchanged: there the response is read on the first `Read()`, where the caller's own deadlines apply.

### Testing

New integration test `TestClientServerTCPResponseTimeout`. The server's outbound blocks forever, so the server never writes a response. The test then checks that `TCP()` returns a `ClosedError`.

- before: `--- FAIL: TestClientServerTCPResponseTimeout (60.01s)` (`TCP()` still blocked when the test's 60s guard fired)
- after: `--- PASS: TestClientServerTCPResponseTimeout (45.01s)`

`go test -count=1 -timeout=5m ./...` in `core` passes (integration tests 109s), `go vet ./...` is clean, `gofumpt -l` reports nothing, and `app` builds.

### Notes

- The test has to wait the full 45s, because the floor is not configurable. I left it at that rather than add a config option only for the test.
- Like any other error on that stream, a timeout makes the reconnectable client replace the whole QUIC connection on the next call. That is the point for a server that has stopped answering. It does also mean a server whose outbound dial takes longer than 45s will now cause a reconnect instead of a hang.

issues.title: fix(client): do not treat stream limit errors as connection closed
issues.body:
Fixes #1714

`wrapIfConnectionClosed` is supposed to let `StreamLimitReachedError` through unchanged and wrap every other error as `ClosedError`. It checks with `errors.Is` against the value `quic.StreamLimitReachedError{}` from `nonPermanentErrors`:

https://github.com/apernet/hysteria/blob/fb25dc852ebbc70658e67889f411887a82b7c281/core/client/client.go#L247-L262

The quic-go fork returns a pointer from `OpenStream`:

https://github.com/apernet/quic-go/blob/a10df75c260c/streams_map_outgoing.go#L76

`*StreamLimitReachedError` never equals the value, and the type has no `Is` method, so the check never matches. The error gets wrapped as `ClosedError`. `reconnectableClientImpl.clientDo` then sets the client to nil without closing it, so a healthy connection is dropped and the next call opens a new one while the old one stays open:

https://github.com/apernet/hysteria/blob/fb25dc852ebbc70658e67889f411887a82b7c281/core/client/reconnect.go#L80-L87

This change matches the pointer with `errors.As`. It also keeps the value check so behaviour doesn't change if a value is ever returned. The now-unused `nonPermanentErrors` list is removed.

Testing: added `TestWrapIfConnectionClosed` in `core/client`. It covers the pointer, the value and a wrapped pointer, and checks that an unrelated error is still wrapped as `ClosedError`. Before the fix, the pointer and wrapped-pointer cases fail (they come back as `ClosedError`). After the fix, the test passes. `go test ./...` in `core` (including integration tests), `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l` are clean.
